title: Sum of Unique Elements
statement: Call an element of the integer array `nums` unique when its value shows up in `nums` one time only. Add up all the unique elements and return the total, which is `0` when `nums` has no unique element.
notes:
## Intuition

Whether a value is unique depends on how many times it occurs in the whole array, not on its neighbours. Comparing every element with every other one answers that in O(n²). Counting each value once in a frequency map answers it for all values at the same time, and then a single pass over the map adds up the values that were seen exactly once.

## Approach

1. Walk through `nums` and increase `count` for each `num`.
2. Start `sum` at `0`.
3. For every entry `[num, times]` in `count`, add `num` to `sum` when `times === 1`.
4. Return `sum`.

## Example 1, step by step

For `nums = [1, 2, 3, 2]` the counts are `1 → 1`, `2 → 2`, `3 → 1`. Value `2` occurs twice and is skipped; `1` and `3` occur once, so `sum = 1 + 3 = 4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass to count and one pass over at most n distinct values.
- Space: O(n) for the map (at most 100 different values here, so an array of size 101 works too).

## Pitfalls

- A repeated value contributes nothing at all, not one copy of itself: `[2, 2, 3]` gives `3`, not `5`.
- Decide uniqueness only after counting the whole array; a value that looks unique halfway may appear again later.
- When every value repeats, return `0`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `count` | map from each value to how many times it occurs |
| `num` | a value of the array |
| `times` | how often `num` occurs |
| `sum` | total of the values that occur exactly once |

narration.2: count will map every value to the number of times it appears.
narration.4: Add one to this value's tally, starting from zero the first time.
narration.7: Look at each distinct value together with its tally.
narration.8: Only a value seen exactly once is unique.
narration.9: Add that unique value to the total.
narration.12: Return the total of the unique values.
